title: The Taster
logline: A tea taster tells a whole estate's story through sight, smell, taste and touch, then gives it a grade: a name built entirely from the senses.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Water carries across: from a well's first water to a tasting room where cups of tea are smelled, tasted and graded, a name built only from the senses.

thread_out.thread: The question of how much we 'know' through the senses moves from the tongue to the eye: at night, a single flame that a crowd sees as a ring.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Everything the tea taster knows about a tea arrives through the senses: its colour, smell, taste and feel. The grade they give is a name gathered from those moments, and the texts describe each moment of knowing as a meeting between a sense and what it senses.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: තේ ගැන රස බලන්නෙකු දන්නා සියල්ල ඇස, නාසය, දිව, කය යන දොරටුවලින් එන අතර, ලබා දෙන ශ්‍රේණිය ඒ දැනීම් එකට ගොනු කළ නමක් පමණි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma sorts experience into twelve sense bases (āyatana): six doors, such as the eye and the tongue, each paired with its own kind of object, such as colour and taste. The texts describe seeing or tasting as arising when a sense meets its object, the way eye-consciousness arises from the eye's sensitivity and a visible form; the bases do not plan this, and knowing simply arises when they meet. A grade is then a name-concept (nāma-paññatti), a name given to what was gathered.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The camera stays close on the taster's ritual: rows of cups, leaf held up and looked at, the loud slurp, the pause while the taste is judged, then a grade written down and called out. The viewer watches an estate's reputation being built from a few seconds of colour, smell and taste, and notices how much of what we 'know' about a thing came in through a door of the senses.

key_terms.en: sense base; 'place' where mind arises and works
sensitive matter (the sensitive surface of eye, ear, and so on)
name-concept: the name that conveys it

lesson.caution: This does not mean taste is only in the eye of the beholder or that the grade is arbitrary; the texts treat sights, smells and tastes as real events, and the point is how knowing happens, not that it cannot be trusted.
lesson.builds_on: The well was named for what is absent; the taster's grade is built entirely from what is present to the senses, turning attention from the named thing to the doors through which it is known.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
